title: EU Climate & Energy Daily Briefing
subtitle: Friday, 10 April 2026 — Key developments from the last 24 hours

items.title: EU Climate Law amendment enters into force — 90% net GHG reduction target for 2040 now legally binding
items.description: Following the provisional political agreement in December 2025, the amended Climate Law now enshrines the EU's 2040 target of 90% net greenhouse gas reduction, with up to 5% contribution from high-quality international credits.

items.title: EU Entry/Exit System (EES) goes live at all Schengen external borders
items.description: The long-awaited Entry/Exit System became fully operational at all external border crossing points of the Schengen area as of 10 April 2026, digitising border checks for non-EU nationals.

items.title: Post-2030 Renewable Energy Framework — public consultation open until 12 June
items.description: The Commission's call for evidence closes 16 April and the full public consultation runs until 12 June 2026, gathering input to shape the next-decade renewable energy legislative framework.

items.title: 235 cross-border energy projects selected to boost Europe's interconnectivity
items.description: The Commission published the second list of Projects of Common and Mutual Interest — 235 projects (up from 166), including 97 electricity/offshore/smart grid projects and 96 hydrogen/electrolyser projects, all eligible for CEF funding.

items.title: EU considers reviving 2022 energy-crisis measures as Iran conflict disrupts markets
items.description: The EU is weighing a return to emergency energy measures — including grid tariff adjustments and tax interventions — similar to those deployed during the 2022 Ukraine crisis, as the ongoing Iran conflict threatens energy supply stability.

items.title: Italy postpones coal plant shutdowns to 2038 — 13 years behind original schedule
items.description: Italy's lower house voted to extend the life of its four remaining coal-fired power plants until 2038, originally scheduled for closure by December 2025 under the National Energy and Climate Plan, citing the Iran-driven energy crisis.

items.title: ETS verified emissions report 2025 due — allowance supply drops 8% year-on-year
items.description: The EU ETS verified emissions report for 2025 is expected by 9 April. Analysts note the 2026 allowance supply will be ~8% lower than 2025, tightening the market and supporting a projected average CO₂ price of €85/t (+18% YoY).

items.title: IRENA: renewables now cheaper than fossil fuels in 91% of new projects worldwide
items.description: IRENA confirms that 91% of new renewable energy projects are now cheaper than fossil fuel alternatives. WindEurope estimates a renewables-based energy system would save Europe €1.6 trillion.

items.title: Global renewable capacity grew 15.5% in 2025 — largest annual increase ever recorded
items.description: Renewables accounted for nearly half of global power capacity by end of 2025, with 692 GW of new capacity added — a 15.5% year-on-year increase, the largest ever recorded.

items.title: EU Taxonomy Climate Delegated Regulation revision — public consultation underway
items.description: The Commission launched a public consultation on revising the Taxonomy Climate Delegated Regulation and Environmental Delegated Act technical screening criteria, targeting adoption in Q2 2026.

items.title: EU ETS carbon price projected to reach €85/t in 2026, crossing €100/t by 2027
items.description: With allowance supply dropping 8% and free allocations for CBAM sectors cut by 2.5%, analysts project the average EU ETS carbon price at €85/t in 2026 (+18% YoY), crossing into triple digits by 2027.

items.title: ESG rating providers face mandatory EU supervision from July 2026
items.description: ESG rating providers operating in the EU will be subject to strict disclosure and supervision requirements starting 2 July 2026, bringing transparency and accountability to a rapidly growing market.

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: US-Iran ceasefire talks set to begin in Islamabad as tensions over Strait of Hormuz persist
items.description: US VP Vance heads to Pakistan for high-stakes negotiations with Iran. The Strait of Hormuz remains restricted, with ADNOC confirming access is 'conditioned and controlled'. Spain's FM urged Iran to negotiate in good faith.

items.title: Israel vows to continue fighting Hezbollah but agrees to direct negotiations with Lebanon
items.description: PM Netanyahu says there is no ceasefire in Lebanon as Israel pursues direct talks on disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations, complicating broader US-Iran diplomacy.

items.title: UN reopens headquarters in Khartoum for first time since 2023 Sudan conflict
items.description: The United Nations reopened its Khartoum headquarters, relocated to Port Sudan in April 2023 when civil war erupted, marking a significant step towards normalisation of international presence in Sudan.
